title: A Gallery of Signals
intro: Every input in the viewer, walked through from its samples to its stability: what the transform is, where its poles, zeros and ROC sit, and what its surface looks like.

blocks.text: Each section below goes through one input of the viewer the way its Next step ▶ walk-through does: the samples, the transform and its ROC, the surface, and what that says about stability and causality. Pick the signal in the viewer as you read.

items: Signal (unit impulse δ[n]): $x[n] = \delta[n]$: 1 at $n = 0$ and 0 everywhere else.
Transform: $X(z) = 1$, ROC: the whole plane. No poles, no zeros.

Surface: A flat surface at height 1 (0 dB). Every frequency passes equally: an impulse contains all frequencies in equal measure. It is the identity of convolution, which is why the transfer function of a system is the transform of its impulse response.
Stability and causality: Stable and causal.
Signal (delayed impulse δ[n−2]): $x[n] = \delta[n-2]$: one sample at $n = 2$.
Transform: $X(z) = z^{-2}$, ROC $z \ne 0$. A double pole at the origin.
Surface: A funnel rising to the origin. On the unit circle $|X| = 1$ at every frequency and the phase is $-2\omega$: a pure delay.
Stability and causality: Stable and causal.
Signal (unit step u[n]): $x[n] = u[n]$: 1 for every $n \ge 0$.
Transform: $X(z) = 1/(1 - z^{-1}) = z/(z - 1)$, ROC $|z| > 1$. A zero at 0 and a pole at 1.

Surface: The pole sits on the unit circle at $\omega = 0$, so the red ring runs right into the plateau there. The step is a constant switched on at $n = 0$: its spectrum has an impulse at $\omega = 0$ and falls off as $1/|2\sin(\omega/2)|$ at other frequencies.
Stability and causality: Causal, not stable: $\sum |u[n]|$ is infinite. Its DTFT exists only as a limit with an impulse at $\omega = 0$.
Signal (decaying exponential rⁿu[n]): $x[n] = r^n u[n]$.
Transform: $X(z) = z/(z - r)$, ROC $|z| > r$. A zero at 0, a pole at $r$.

Surface: One peak on the positive real axis. For $0 < r < 1$ the response is largest at $\omega = 0$, $1/(1 - r)$, and smallest at $180°$, $1/(1 + r)$: a low-pass filter. With $r = 0.8$ that is 5 (14 dB) against 0.56 (−5.1 dB).
Stability and causality: Causal; stable when $|r| < 1$.
Signal (left-sided exponential −rⁿu[−n−1]): $x[n] = -r^n u[-n-1]$: $-r^n$ for $n \le -1$.
Transform: $X(z) = z/(z - r)$ again, but ROC $|z| < r$.
Surface: The same surface as the decaying exponential, solid inside the pole instead of outside it.
Stability and causality: Not causal. Stable only when $r > 1$, so that the ROC $|z| < r$ reaches past the unit circle: then the samples shrink as $n \to -\infty$.
Signal (two-sided exponential r^|n|): $x[n] = r^{|n|}$, decaying both ways.
Transform: $X(z) = (1 - r^2) z / ((z - r)(1 - r z))$, ROC $r < |z| < 1/r$. Poles at $r$ and $1/r$.

Surface: Two peaks, mirror images through the unit circle, with the ring of convergence between them. The response on the circle is real and positive: the signal is symmetric in time, so it has zero phase.
Stability and causality: Stable for $r < 1$, not causal. For $r \ge 1$ there is no ROC.
Signal (ramped exponential n·rⁿu[n]): $x[n] = n r^n u[n]$.
Transform: $X(z) = r z / (z - r)^2$, ROC $|z| > r$. A double pole at $r$.
Surface: One peak, steeper than a single pole's: in decibels a double pole rises twice as fast. In time the signal rises, then decays.
Stability and causality: Causal; stable when $|r| < 1$.
Signal (damped cosine rⁿcos(θn)u[n]): $x[n] = r^n \cos(\theta n) u[n]$.
Transform: $X(z) = z(z - r\cos\theta)/(z^2 - 2r\cos\theta\, z + r^2)$, ROC $|z| > r$. Poles $r e^{\pm j\theta}$, zeros at 0 and $r\cos\theta$.
Surface: Two peaks at angles $\pm\theta$. As $r \to 1$ the response peaks sharply near $\omega = \theta$.
Stability and causality: Causal; stable when $r < 1$.
Signal (damped sine rⁿsin(θn)u[n]): $x[n] = r^n \sin(\theta n) u[n]$.
Transform: $X(z) = r\sin\theta\, z/(z^2 - 2r\cos\theta\, z + r^2)$, ROC $|z| > r$. The same poles, one zero at 0.

Surface: Almost the cosine's surface. The poles, which set the ringing, are the same; only the zeros differ, and they set the starting phase of the oscillation. At $\theta = 0$ or $180°$ the sine is zero for every $n$, and so is $X(z)$.
Stability and causality: Causal; stable when $r < 1$.
Signal (8-sample pulse u[n]−u[n−8]): $x[n] = 1$ for $n = 0, \ldots, 7$.
Transform: $X(z) = (1 - z^{-8})/(1 - z^{-1})$, ROC $z \ne 0$. Seven zeros on the unit circle, seven poles at 0.
Surface: A plateau at the origin and seven pits round the circle at multiples of $45°$. The response is 8 at $\omega = 0$ and has lobes between the pits.
Stability and causality: Stable and causal, like every finite causal signal.
Signal (notch filter δ[n]−2cosθ·δ[n−1]+δ[n−2]): $x[n] = \delta[n] - 2\cos\theta\, \delta[n-1] + \delta[n-2]$.
Transform: $X(z) = (z - e^{j\theta})(z - e^{-j\theta})/z^2$, ROC $z \ne 0$. Zeros on the circle at $\pm\theta$, a double pole at 0.
Surface: Two pits on the unit circle at $\pm\theta$: the response is exactly 0 at $\omega = \theta$.
Stability and causality: Stable and causal.
$\delta[n] \leftrightarrow 1$, every $z$.
$\delta[n - k] \leftrightarrow z^{-k}$, $z \ne 0$ for $k > 0$.
$a^n u[n] \leftrightarrow 1/(1 - a z^{-1})$, $|z| > |a|$.
$-a^n u[-n-1] \leftrightarrow 1/(1 - a z^{-1})$, $|z| < |a|$.
$n a^n u[n] \leftrightarrow a z^{-1}/(1 - a z^{-1})^2$, $|z| > |a|$.
$r^n \cos(\theta n) u[n] \leftrightarrow (1 - r\cos\theta\, z^{-1})/(1 - 2r\cos\theta\, z^{-1} + r^2 z^{-2})$, $|z| > r$.
$r^n \sin(\theta n) u[n] \leftrightarrow r\sin\theta\, z^{-1}/(1 - 2r\cos\theta\, z^{-1} + r^2 z^{-2})$, $|z| > r$.

blocks.title: Match the surface
blocks.text: A surface has one plateau on the positive real axis at 0.6, a pit at the origin, and is solid outside the circle $|z| = 0.6$. Which signal is it, and what is its response at $\omega = 0$?
solution: One pole at 0.6, one zero at 0, ROC outside: $0.6^n u[n]$. At $\omega = 0$, $|X| = 1/(1 - 0.6) = 2.5$.
